summary_paragraphs: You were in the heart hospital (Klinik für Kardiologie, Krankenhaus XYZ) from 22.06.2022 until 24.06.2022. The reason was your known coronary heart disease. This means the arteries of your heart are narrowed.

On 23.06.2022 the doctors did a heart catheter test. They found narrowing in three heart arteries. They widened one artery on the right side of your heart and put in a small metal tube called a stent (Promus ELITE 2.75 x 12 mm). The blood flow after the procedure was good.

The letter says the recovery after the procedure was without problems. At discharge you had no complaints. The doctors ask you to keep taking ASS and Clopidogrel together until May 2023. After that, take ASS alone for life.

Because of the contrast dye used in the test and your weak kidneys, the doctors ask you to drink 1.5 to 2 litres of fluid each day. Your kidney test showed GFR 36 ml/min, which means your kidneys work less well than normal. Your heart rhythm test (EKG) on 22.06.2022 was normal.

medicines.note: Blood thinner. To be taken for life.

medicines.name: Clopidogrel Zentiva 75 mg
medicines.note: Second blood thinner. Only until 05/2023, then stop (as per letter).

medicines.name: Pantoprazol PUREN 20 mg
medicines.note: Protects the stomach. Take before meals.

jargon.plain: The arteries that feed the heart muscle are narrowed.
A test where a thin tube goes into the heart arteries. Narrowed parts can be widened, often with a small metal tube (stent).
A small metal mesh tube placed in an artery to keep it open. It slowly gives off medicine.
Narrowing in three of the heart arteries.
Taking two blood thinners together (here ASS and Clopidogrel) to prevent blood clots in the stent.
The kidneys work less well than normal, medium stage.
A kidney test number. Lower numbers mean weaker kidneys.
Getting short of breath when doing bigger physical effort.
A long-term lung illness that makes breathing harder.
High blood pressure that needs treatment.
Normal, regular heartbeat at 71 beats per minute.
Blood flows fully through the artery again. This is the best result.

faq.q: Why did I get a stent?
faq.a: Because one of your heart arteries was narrowed. The stent keeps it open so blood can flow.

faq.q: How long must I take Clopidogrel?
faq.a: Until the end of May 2023. After that, ASS alone for life. Do not stop earlier without asking your doctor.

faq.q: Why should I drink 1.5 to 2 litres a day?
faq.a: Because of the contrast dye from the procedure and your weak kidneys. It helps protect the kidneys.
In about 6 months. The exact date is not in the letter. Ask your heart doctor's office.

faq.q: Was everything okay when I left?
faq.a: Yes. The letter says the recovery had no problems and you were free of complaints.

faq.q: What if I feel unwell at home?
faq.a: The letter does not give special warning signs. In general, get help quickly for chest pain or strong breathlessness.
